name: Istanbul
tagline: Ottoman cuisine with a Michelin star inside the Spice Bazaar, since 1901.

Pandeli.description: Ottoman cuisine inside the Grand Spice Bazaar since 1901. Michelin star, reviewed by critic Manos Angelakis (LuxuryWeb Magazine).

Tatbak.description: Istanbul's benchmark kebab since 1960, with spicy Gaziantep-style lahmacun.

Tarihi Karaköy Balıkçısı.description: A historic fish restaurant in Karaköy, serving since 1923 at the entrance to Griffin Han.

Kızılkayalar.description: The Beyoğlu spot behind the islak hamburger (wet burger) that Anthony Bourdain tried on "No Reservations": "Why on earth do Turks go to McDonald's when they have this?"

Sofyalı 9.description: One of Beyoğlu's most established traditional meyhanes, with mezze and raki near Tünel.

Türk Fatih Tutak.description: Contemporary Turkish tasting-menu cuisine holding two Michelin stars in the Bomonti district; chef Fatih Tutak reinterprets Anatolian techniques with fine-dining precision.

Mikla.description: Atop the Marmara Pera hotel, chef Mehmet Gürs blends Anatolian and Scandinavian cooking with views over the Golden Horn. One Michelin star.

Neolokal.description: Inside the Salt Galata cultural center, chef Maksut Aşkar reinvents Anatolian recipes using produce from small Turkish producers. One Michelin star.

Araka.description: A small restaurant in Yeniköy serving vegetable-forward modern Turkish cuisine, led by chef Zeynep Pınar Taşdemir. One Michelin star.

Arkestra.description: Set in a restored 1960s villa in Etiler, chef Cenk Debensason blends classic French technique with global influences. One Michelin star.

Nicole.description: On the terrace of Tomtom Suites with views over the historic peninsula, chef Serkan Aksoy signs a contemporary Anatolian menu. One Michelin star.

Sankai by Nagaya.description: A 24-seat Japanese restaurant in the historic Bebek Hotel, a partnership between chef Yoshizumi Nagaya and a Turkish entrepreneur. One Michelin star.

Casa Lavanda.description: In the coastal district of Şile on Istanbul's outskirts, this restaurant grows most of its own produce in its garden. Michelin star since 2025.

Karaköy Lokantası.description: Opened in 2007 by Oral Kurt and Aylin Okutan, this Karaköy neighborhood classic gives a modern twist to traditional Turkish cooking. Michelin Bib Gourmand.

Ali Ocakbaşı.description: A Turkish grill house (ocakbaşı) with views in Karaköy, known for its charcoal-grilled lamb skewers. Michelin Bib Gourmand.

Araf İstanbul.description: An intimate chef's-table restaurant in Kadıköy founded by Kenan and Pınar Çetinkaya, centered on open-fire cooking. Michelin Bib Gourmand in 2024 and 2025.

Efendy.description: A Levent restaurant specializing in Anatolian regional recipes rarely found elsewhere in the city. Michelin Bib Gourmand.

Çiya Sofrası.description: Chef Musa Dağdeviren revives forgotten recipes from across Anatolia at his Kadıköy restaurant, featured in the Istanbul episode of Netflix's 'Chef's Table'.

Balıkçı Sabahattin.description: A benchmark fish house in Sultanahmet, tucked in an alley by the old sea walls, serving fish mezze and the day's catch for decades.

Hamdi Restaurant.description: Perched above the Spice Bazaar in Eminönü with views of the Golden Horn; chef Hamdi arrived from Urfa in the 1960s to popularize southeastern Turkish kebab.

Develi Restaurant.description: Founded in Gaziantep in 1912 and in Samatya since 1966, it's famed for its pistachio kebab and has hosted many Turkish artists and politicians.

Beyti Restaurant.description: A meat institution in Florya since 1945, with 500 seats and the oak-charcoal-grilled Beyti kebab (wrapped in thin flatbread) that bears its name.

Zübeyir Ocakbaşı.description: An open grill house near Taksim since 2006, serving lamb skewers and Gaziantep salad cooked in full view of diners over the ocakbaşı coals.

Sultanahmet Köftecisi Selim Usta.description: On Divanyolu, in the shadow of Hagia Sophia, it has served its iconic flat grilled köfte with piyaz bean salad since 1920, now run by the fourth generation.

Şehzade Cağ Kebap.description: A specialist in cağ kebabı, the horizontal spit-roasted lamb kebab from Erzurum served in thin slices with lavaş bread, near Sirkeci station.

Karaköy Güllüoğlu.description: Istanbul's most reputed baklava, in Karaköy since 1949; it also makes kadayıf and other syrup pastries following the Güllü family recipe.

Hafız Mustafa 1864.description: An Ottoman patisserie founded in 1864 during the reign of Sultan Abdülaziz, celebrated for its baklava, milk puddings, and Turkish delight.

Vefa Bozacısı.description: Founded in 1876, this boza (fermented wheat drink) shop still displays the glass Atatürk drank from during his 1937 visit.

Van Kahvaltı Evi.description: In Cihangir, it serves the elaborate breakfast spread of Turkey's eastern Van region — cheeses, honeys, and otvot — following that area's traditional breakfast ritual.

Mandabatmaz.description: A tiny spot down a Beyoğlu alley famous for its exceptionally thick-foamed Turkish coffee, brewed the traditional way for generations.

Fazıl Bey'in Türk Kahvesi.description: In Kadıköy's historic market, it roasts its own beans and serves a thick Turkish coffee considered among the city's best.

Baylan Pastanesi.description: A French-style patisserie in Kadıköy famed for its Kup Griye dessert — ice cream, caramel, pistachio, and Chantilly cream — served in its back garden.

Pierre Loti Café.cuisine: Turkish / tea and coffee with a view
Pierre Loti Café.description: A historic café on Eyüp hill above the Golden Horn, reached by cable car; frequented by 19th-century French writer Pierre Loti.

Asitane Restaurant.description: Next to the Chora Church, since 1991 it has rigorously revived recipes from Ottoman palace archives, many long vanished from today's cuisine.

Dürümzade.description: A small takeaway spot in Beyoğlu renowned for its lamb dürüm wrapped in freshly baked lavaş bread; featured by Anthony Bourdain on 'No Reservations'.

Sur Ocakbaşı.description: In the Zeyrek neighborhood, it serves büryan — lamb slow-cooked in an underground pit oven, a Bitlis specialty — which Anthony Bourdain tried on 'No Reservations'.

Karpi Pide-Köfte.description: On the Asian shore in Beylerbeyi, it serves Black Sea-style pide that Anthony Bourdain ate on 'Parts Unknown' with photographer Marat Germen.

Poyraz Sahil Balık.description: A seaside restaurant in Poyrazköy, at the northern mouth of the Bosphorus, serving fish caught the same day by local fishermen.

Hacı Abdullah Restaurant.description: Founded in 1888 in Karaköy under a license from Sultan Abdülhamid II, now in Beyoğlu; celebrated for its stews, fruit preserves, and pickles.

Nusr-Et Steakhouse.description: Nusret Gökçe's ('Salt Bae') original Etiler steakhouse, birthplace in 2010 of his viral salt-sprinkling gesture, now a global social-media phenomenon.

360 Istanbul.description: A rooftop restaurant atop the historic Mısır building on İstiklal Street, with panoramic 360-degree views and a menu blending local and global flavors.

Sunset Grill & Bar.description: Above Ulus Park with Bosphorus views, it has combined Mediterranean and Japanese cooking since 1994; a member of the Chaîne des Rôtisseurs.

Kanaat Lokantası.description: In Üsküdar since 1933, this esnaf lokanta serves traditional Ottoman dishes by weight, an unchanged classic on the Asian shore.

Namlı Gurme.description: Turkey's pioneering deli-with-restaurant concept, in Karaköy; cheeses, cured meats, olives, and an extensive Turkish breakfast.

Divan Pastanesi.description: The patisserie of the Divan Hotel, opened in 1956 in Elmadağ; it produces tons of handcrafted chocolates and lokum, a benchmark for chocolate in Turkey.

Feriye Lokantası.description: In the historic Feriye Palace by the Bosphorus in Ortaköy, it has reinterpreted rich Ottoman culinary tradition since opening in 1995.

Tuğra Restaurant.description: In Çırağan Palace (now the Kempinski hotel) overlooking the Bosphorus, it recreates recipes from Ottoman palace archives amid marble columns.

Krependeki İmroz.description: One of the oldest meyhanes on Nevizade Street, opened in 1941 with Greek-Istanbulite roots, serving fish mezze and rakı.

Fıccın.description: A small meyhane in Asmalı Mescit specializing in Circassian cooking, with its namesake meat pastry and Circassian chicken beloved by locals.

Şark Kahvesi.description: A traditional coffeehouse inside the Grand Bazaar, an Ottoman-decorated refuge for merchants and visitors since the mid-20th century.

Konyalı Restaurant.description: Founded in 1897, it has served inside Topkapı Palace since 1969, with Bosphorus views and traditional Ottoman dishes.

Havuzlu Restaurant.description: Opened in 1959, it was the Grand Bazaar's first and largest restaurant; it serves mantı, kebabs, and Ottoman stews under historic vaulted ceilings.

Erzincanlı Ali Baba.description: Facing the Süleymaniye Mosque since 1924, it serves a single dish — kuru fasulye white beans cooked in a copper pot over charcoal — with rice and pickles.

Meze by Lemon Tree.description: Facing the Pera Palace hotel, it reinvents traditional Turkish meze with contemporary technique, among Beyoğlu's most praised meyhanes.

Çengelköy İskele Restaurant.description: By the Çengelköy pier on the Asian shore, with views of the Bosphorus Bridge and a menu focused exclusively on fish and seafood.

Borsa Lokantası.description: Opened in 1927 in Eminönü, next to the old grain exchange that gave it its name; now with several branches, it still serves home-style Ottoman cooking.

Ali Muhiddin Hacı Bekir.description: Turkey's oldest confectionery shop, opened in Eminönü in 1777; its founder is credited with creating the modern lokum, or 'Turkish delight'.

Adem Baba.description: An unpretentious seafood institution in Arnavutköy by the Bosphorus; it serves no alcohol, but its mezze and fresh fish draw daily lines.

Yeni Lokanta.description: Since 2013, chef Civan Er has given a light, contemporary twist to traditional Turkish cooking, with an emphasis on vegetables, local produce, and Turkish wine.

Çiçek Pasajı.description: A 19th-century arcade on İstiklal Street, now lined with meyhanes offering shared tables, live music, and rakı — a symbol of Beyoğlu nightlife.
